text:
sasha: quick heads-up — bringing up GemmaX-14B-ffn with the new rotary-scale tweak. I ran the standard onboarding evals and saw a weird drift in embedding nearest neighbors for the tokenized prefix tests. :thinking:

omar: can you paste the diffs? is this after quant or before?

sasha: happens before quant too. it looks like the vocab mapping changed for a handful of rare tokens (we added a tokenizer patch yesterday). small offsets but large neighbor changes. sample: `"token_ħ": was id 5873, now 5874` — basically a +1 shift in a contiguous block.

becca: ugh, that can cascade into kvcache misalignment if rotary/kvcache indexing expects the old ids. did you check kvcache tests?

sasha: yes, ran quick kvcache smoke. no panics, but attention alignment metrics drop ~3-5% on long context synthetic prompts (16k).

chandra: do we have a reproducible script for the embed nearest-neighbor check? I can run on dedicated.

sasha: yupp: `python tools/compare_embeds.py --ref outputs/gemmax_v1/emb.npz --cand outputs/gemmax_v2/emb.npz --k 10 --metrics nn_overlap,cos_sim`

sasha: output snippet:
```
nn_overlap@k=10: 0.82 -> 0.58
median_cos_sim: 0.93 -> 0.73
affected_tokens: 112
example_token: "ŝain" ref_rank=3 cand_rank=987
```

omar: that overlap drop is consistent with a small token id permutation. could be tokenizer reorder + vocab.json reindexing. any diffs in the tokenizer repo?

becca: @chandra the tokenizer commit 9a7d introduced `preserve_uncommon_tokens` that reserializes the vocab with deterministic sorting by string. if previously the build used binary order we might shift ids.

chandra: confirmed. build logs: `scripts/build_vocab.py` changed sort key. So model weights were exported with the old id mapping but the new tokenizer gives different ids. That matches.

eval-bot: CI: onboarding/evals/gemmax-vocab-check FAILED (nn_overlap < 0.7) — see: https://ci.redwood/gemmabase/1825001234/report

omar: two paths: reexport tokenizer with old mapping, or remap the embedding matrix and kvcache indices to new vocab order. remap involves permuting embedding rows + any token-indexed caches in checkpoints.

becca: remap looks safer for long term (keeps tokenizer deterministic sorted). I sketched a remap script last quarter. sasha, can you run remap on a small checkpoint and rerun the compare?

sasha: starting a run on dedicated. remap command:
```
python tools/remap_checkpoint.py --ckpt ckpt/gemmax_v1.pt --vmap old_vocab.json new_vocab.json --out ckpt/gemmax_v1-remapped.pt
```

sasha: quick note — need to remap both `tok_embeddings.weight` and `lm_head.weight` (tied) plus any saved `past_key_values` if they include token-indexed buffers (they don't in our format, just position-based). Also update tokenizer metadata version.

chandra: also watch rotary params: we had a small rotary_scale experiment (0.95->1.0) merged in the same branch. if we change rotary scale and remap vocab simultaneously it will be harder to attribute. do them separately.

sasha: good catch. i'll revert the rotary tweak locally and only do vocab remap for parity. running remap now (est ~12m).

omar: once done, please run `python tools/compare_attention.py --ckpt ...` and `pytest tests/embeddings/test_nearest.py::TestNN::test_k10` on the same host.

(eval-bot): job remap/1825001234 started on dedicated-3 (ETA 12m) :hourglass_flowing_sand:

becca: if remap fixes nn_overlap, we still need to run quant experiments (int8/llm-int8) because remapping can expose sensitivity in quant kernels due to reordering cache warming patterns.

sasha: noted. plan: 1) remap & re-run nn checks 2) re-enable rotary tweak in isolation and run longcontext attention regression tests 3) quantize and run quality regression evals. will post results in this thread.

omar: thanks. tagging @infra to keep an eye on dedicated capacity usage for the quant runs. :eyes:
